rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa says كفلين (two shares) means a doubling of reward in Abyssinian.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص، عن أبي موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says ناشئة الليل is Abyssinian usage for a man rising at night; they say نشأ.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة
rows.claim: Abu Maysara explains أوبي معه as “glorify with him” in Abyssinian.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي ميسرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says قسورة means lion in Arabic, shar in Persian, aryā in Nabataean, and qaswara in Abyssinian.
rows.anchor: عن يوسف بن مهران، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that Quraysh asked why the Quran was not revealed in both foreign and Arabic speech, and cites God's response in 41:44.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر بن أبي المغيرة، عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id says the Quran contains words from other languages, including sijjil, a Persian expression arabized from sang (stone) and clay.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر بن أبي المغيرة، عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud twice praises Ibn Abbas as an excellent interpreter of the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان، عن مسلم، قال: قال عبد الله: «نعم ترجمان القرآن ابن عباس»

rows.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Mulayka saw Mujahid ask Ibn Abbas for Quran interpretation while Ibn Abbas told him to write, until Mujahid had asked about all of it.
rows.anchor: عن عثمان المكي، عن ابن أبي مليكة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says he presented the whole codex to Ibn Abbas three times, stopping at every verse to ask its interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «عرضت المصحف على ابن عباس، ثلاث عرضات، من فاتحته إلى خاتمته، أوقفته عند كل آية منه، وأسأله عنها»

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says Mujahid's interpretation is sufficient when it reaches a reader.
rows.anchor: سمعت سفيان الثوري، يقول: «إذا جاءك التفسير عن مجاهد، فحسبك به»

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن ميسرة
rows.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn Maysara says al-Dahhak never met Ibn Abbas; he met Sa'id ibn Jubayr in Rayy and took tafsir from him.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن ميسرة، قال: «لم يلق الضحاك ابن عباس، وإنما لقي سعيد بن جبير بالري، وأخذ عنه التفسير»

rows.speaker: مشاش
rows.claim: Mishash reports that when he asked al-Dahhak whether he had heard anything from Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak said no.
rows.anchor: عن شعبة، عن مشاش، قال: قلت للضحاك

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi rebuked Abu Salih Badhan for interpreting the Quran when he could not read it.
rows.anchor: كان الشعبي يمر بأبي صالح باذان، فيأخذ بأذنه فيعركها، ويقول: «تفسر القرآن وأنت لا تقرأ القرآن»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's judging with truth as His ability to repay good with good and evil with evil; He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
rows.anchor: حدثنا الأعمش، قال: حدثني سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi's version adds that God rewards a good deed tenfold, unlike the version from Ibn Abbas that gives good for good and evil for evil.
rows.anchor: حدثني به الكلبي إلا أنه قال: «إن الله قادر أن يجزي بالسيئة السيئة، وبالحسنة عشرا»

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash says that if al-Kalbi's report were his own, he would not give it away for something worthless.
rows.anchor: فقال الأعمش: لو أن الذي عند الكلبي

rows.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jundub warned Talq ibn Habib away after Talq asked him about a Quran verse, adjuring him to leave if he was Muslim.
rows.anchor: جندب بن عبد الله فسأله عن آية من القرآن فقال له

rows.speaker: يزيد بن أبي يزيد
rows.claim: Yazid says people asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib about lawful and unlawful matters, which he knew best, but he stayed silent when they asked for a verse's interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال: «كنا نسأل سعيد بن المسيب عن الحلال والحرام وكان، أعلم الناس، وإذا سألناه عن تفسير آية من القرآن، سكت كأن لم يسمع»

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: When asked to interpret a verse, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said to ask someone who claimed that nothing in it was hidden from him, meaning Ikrima.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن المسيب عن آية من القرآن، فقال

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says he had asked about every verse but insists that interpretation is a matter of transmitted report from God.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي: «والله ما من آية إلا قد سألت عنها، ولكنها الرواية عن الله»

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says he would not speak about the Quran, the spirit, opinion, or similar matters before his death.
rows.anchor: حدثني رجل، عن الشعبي، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari distinguishes matters whose interpretation God alone knows from matters God taught the Prophet for people through revelation; the Prophet learned through Gabriel or another messenger.
rows.anchor: ومن أي القرآن، ما قد ذكرنا أن الله جل ثناؤه، استأثر بعلم تأويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's revealed explanations cover necessary commands, prohibitions, lawful and unlawful matters, duties, and religious law whose wording is general; God taught him to clarify revelation, as 16:44 says.
rows.anchor: فقال له جل ذكره: {وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم ولعلهم يتفكرون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari rejects reading the report that the Prophet interpreted only a few verses as saying he explained only a tiny portion; it concerns verses whose interpretation requires his revealed explanation.
rows.anchor: ولو كان تأويل الخبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان لا يفسر من القرآن شيئا إلا آيا تعد هو ما يسبق إليه أوهام أهل الغباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari rejects the claim that the seven ahruf are seven separate languages scattered across the Quran: that cannot explain reports of companions disputing a sura's recitation and being told to read as taught.
rows.anchor: وفي صحة الخبر عن الذين روي عنهم الاختلاف في حروف القرآن، على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فإنهم اختلفوا وتحاكموا إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reports explain the variant letters through synonymous wording, such as “come,” “approach,” and Ibn Mas'ud's “illa zaqiyya” for “illa sayha.”
rows.anchor: وأن بعضهم قال: هو بمنزلة قراءة عبد الله: «إلا زقية» ، وهي في قراءتنا: {إلا صيحة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari holds that the seven ahruf are different expressions in one word or letter with the same meaning, like a set of Arabic synonyms.
rows.anchor: بل الأحرف السبعة التي أنزل الله بها القرآن هن لغات سبع في حرف واحد وكلمة واحدة، باختلاف الألفاظ واتفاق المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari clarifies that he does not claim all seven variant wordings can be found in the Quran's present written form; he explains the Prophet's saying according to the reports.
rows.anchor: إنا لم ندع أن ذلك موجود اليوم، وإنما أخبرنا أن معنى قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six unused ahruf were neither abrogated nor forgotten: the community was allowed to preserve and read any one of the seven, analogous to choosing one of three expiations for a broken oath.
rows.anchor: لم تنسخ فترفع، ولا ضيعتها الأمة، وهي مأمورة بحفظها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet names the Fatiha Umm al-Quran, Fatiha al-Kitab, and the seven oft-repeated verses.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «هي أم القرآن، هي فاتحة الكتاب، وهي السبع المثاني»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called Fatiha al-Kitab because it opens the written codex and prayer recitation, and precedes the other suras in reading and writing.
rows.anchor: وسميت فاتحة الكتاب، لأنها يفتتح بكتابتها المصاحف، ويقرأ بها في الصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm al-Quran means the leading, encompassing source; Arabs call a thing that gathers and leads its related parts an umm, such as the head's covering or an army banner.
rows.anchor: لتسمية العرب كل جامع أمرا أو مقدما لأمر، إذا كانت له توابع تتبعه، هو لها إمام جامع أما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's banner poem uses umm for the standard that gathers the group under it when they travel or meet an enemy.
rows.anchor: على رأسه أم لنا نقتدي بها … جماع أمور لا نعاصي لها أمرا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Mecca is called Umm al-Qura either because it precedes and gathers the settlements, or because the earth was spread from it as their mother.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن مكة سميت أم القرى، لتقدمها أمام جميعها، وجمعها ما سواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humayd ibn Thawr calls fifty the mother of numbers below it because it encompasses them.
rows.anchor: لأن الخمسين جامعة ما دونها من العدد، فسماها أما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All reciters and scholars agree the Fatiha consists of seven verses, but disagree whether the basmala counts and which verse is seventh.
rows.anchor: فإنها سبع آيات، لا خلاف بين الجميع من القراء والعلماء في ذلك، وإنما اختلفوا في الآي التي صارت بها سبع آيات

rows.speaker: أعظم أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The majority of Kufans count the basmala among the seven verses; this view is also reported from Companions and Successors.
rows.anchor: أعظم أهل الكوفة: صارت سبع آيات

rows.speaker: أعظم قراء أهل المدينة ومتفقهيهم
rows.claim: The majority of Medinan reciters and jurists exclude the basmala and count “those upon whom You bestowed favor” as the seventh verse.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي سبع آيات، وليس منهن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، ولكن السابعة أنعمت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari says he has already briefly stated his correct view elsewhere and will fully relate the disagreement in a larger legal work, without restating his choice here.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وقد بينا الصواب من القول عندنا في ذلك، في كتابنا اللطيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha is called the oft-repeated because it is recited in every obligatory and voluntary prayer; Hasan al-Basri interpreted it this way.
rows.anchor: فلأنها تثنى قراءتها في كل صلاة تطوع ومكتوبة، وكذلك كان الحسن البصري يتأول ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited Arabic verse fragment, kitab means “written.”
rows.anchor: كتاب مثل ما لصق الغراء. يعني به مكتوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr may mean a reminder from God that teaches servants His limits, duties, and wisdom, or honor and renown for believers.
rows.anchor: وأما تأويل اسمه الذي هو الذكر، فإنه محتمل معنيين: أحدهما أنه ذكر من الله جل ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari reads “a reminder for you and your people” in 43:44 as honor and renown for the Prophet and his people.
rows.anchor: يعني به أنه شرف له ولقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari says the names of Quran suras were given by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ثم لسور القرآن أسماء سماها بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Wathila ibn al-Asqa' reports the Prophet's mapping: the seven long suras replace the Torah, the mi'un the Psalms, the mathani the Gospel, and the Mufassal is an added distinction.
rows.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطول، وأعطيت مكان الزبور المئين، وأعطيت مكان الإنجيل المثاني، وفضلت بالمفصل»

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba reports the Prophet mapping the seven long suras to the Torah, mathani to the Psalms, mi'un to the Gospel, and Mufassal as a special favor.
rows.anchor: عن أبي قلابة، قال: قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: خالد
rows.claim: Khalid says people called the Mufassal “the Arabic”; some said there is no prostration in the Arabic (Mufassal).
rows.anchor: قال خالد: كانوا يسمون المفصل: العربي؛ قال خالد: قال بعضهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud compares the long suras to the Torah, the mi'un to the Gospel, the mathani to the Psalms, and says the remainder exceeds the other books.
rows.anchor: عن المسيب، عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report from Wathila says God gave the Prophet the seven long suras for the Torah, mathani for the Gospel, mi'un for the Psalms, and favored him with Mufassal.
rows.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «أعطاني ربي مكان التوراة السبع الطول، ومكان الإنجيل المثاني، ومكان الزبور المئين، وفضلني بالمفصل»

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Bakra reports that Gabriel asked the Prophet to recite on one letter, Michael urged him to request more, and the allowance rose to six or seven; the forms are sufficient if mercy and punishment verses are not mismatched.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة، عن أبيه، قال: قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari says the seven ahruf differ in wording while agreeing in meaning, like hallum and ta'al, rather than differing in meanings that change legal rulings.
rows.anchor: فقد أوضح نص هذا الخبر أن اختلاف الأحرف السبعة، إنما هو اختلاف ألفاظ، كقولك هلم وتعال

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says the reciters he heard were close in their readings, so people should read as taught and avoid affectation, like saying hallum or ta'al.
rows.anchor: عن شقيق، قال، قال عبد الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says anyone who reads on a letter should not switch; he adds that he would seek someone more knowledgeable than himself about God's Book.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عمن سمع ابن مسعود، يقول: «من قرأ منكم على حرف، فلا يتحولن

rows.speaker: رجل من أصحاب عبد الله
rows.claim: An unnamed companion of Abdullah reports his instruction that anyone who reads on a letter should not move to another.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عابس، عن رجل من أصحاب عبد الله، عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari explains “letter” here as a person's recitation or reading, a usage like naming a poem a poet's “word,” rather than switching among Quran topics or alphabet characters.
rows.anchor: وإنما عنى رحمة الله عليه، أن من قرأ بحرفه، وحرفه: قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reader should not abandon a Companion's reading from one of the seven ahruf out of aversion; rejecting any one of them amounts to rejecting the whole Quran.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بحرف أبي، أو بحرف زيد، أو بحرف بعض من قرأ من أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari says disbelief in one letter, meaning a transmitted reading among the seven, is disbelief in all of it.
rows.anchor: فإن الكفر ببعضه كفر بجميعه، والكفر بحرف من ذلك كفر بجميعه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi harshly rebuked al-Suddi for interpreting, saying that being beaten with a drum would be better than attending his session.
rows.anchor: مر الشعبي على السدي وهو يفسر، فقال: «لأن يضرب على استك بالطبل

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i remarks that al-Suddi interprets according to the interpretations of the people.
rows.anchor: عن مسلم بن عبد الرحمن النخعي، قال: كنت مع إبراهيم، فرأى السدي، فقال: «أما إنه يفسر تفسير القوم»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says he knows no one who can keep pace with al-Kalbi in Quran interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «ما أرى أحدا يجري مع الكلبي في التفسير في عنان»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabari divides interpretation into what God alone knows (such as the Hour and other future events), what God taught His Messenger for people through revelation, and Arabic meanings accessible to speakers of the Quran's language.
rows.anchor: وأن تأويل جميع القرآن على أوجه ثلاثة: أحدها: لا سبيل إلى الوصول إليه، وهو الذي استأثر الله بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For meanings entrusted to the Prophet, the soundest interpretation relies on established Prophetic reports, whether widely transmitted, carried by reliable narrators, or supported by clear evidence.
rows.anchor: أوضحهم حجة فيما تأول وفسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For interpretations reached through Arabic, Tabari calls for the clearest proof from circulating Arabic poetry or ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: وأوضحهم برهانا فيما ترجم وبين من ذلك، مما كان مدركا علمه من جهة اللسان، إما بالشواهد من أشعارهم السائرة
